The Numbers Don't Lie: Nintendo's Evolution from Couch Co-op to the Switch Era

thread // May 20, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Read more on Threads

The numbers don't lie. 📊

I tracked Nintendo's evolution from the golden era of '90s and 2000s couch co-op to the modern juggernauts of the Switch generation. When I posted this, the original Switch had passed 155 million units, and the Switch 2 was already out of the gate with nearly 20 million sold.

Here's how every Nintendo home console stacks up.

The home console scoreboard

Lifetime units sold worldwide, from Nintendo's own figures:

  • NES (1983): 61.91 million
  • Super Nintendo (1990): 49.10 million
  • Nintendo 64 (1996): 32.93 million
  • GameCube (2001): 21.74 million
  • Wii (2006): 101.63 million
  • Wii U (2012): 13.56 million
  • Switch (2017): 156.59 million and counting
  • Switch 2 (2025): 23.68 million and counting

Years are the original Japanese launches, and the Switch numbers are as of June 30, 2026.

The couch co-op era

The N64 and GameCube never sold like the NES or the Wii, but ask anybody who grew up with them: four controller ports changed everything. GoldenEye, Mario Kart 64, Mario Party, Super Smash Bros. Melee, Double Dash: that era was built around everybody in the same room, yelling at the same screen.

Then the Wii took that idea to the whole family and sold more than 100 million consoles doing it.

The Wii U stumble and the Switch comeback

The Wii U is the reminder that Nintendo can miss. At 13.56 million, it's Nintendo's lowest-selling home console. But the Switch answered it by combining home console and handheld, and it became Nintendo's best-selling console ever, passing the Nintendo DS's 154.02 million.

The Switch 2 is moving fast

The Switch 2 launched in June 2025 and passed the GameCube's entire lifetime total in about 13 months. Nintendo expects to sell 16.5 million more this fiscal year.

Update (September 2026)

As of June 30, 2026, Nintendo reported 23.68 million Switch 2 units and 156.59 million for the original Switch. The Switch 2's U.S. price also went up on September 1, from $449.99 to $499.99.

Sources: Nintendo Life, VGChartz, Variety

Quick answers

What is Nintendo's best-selling console? The Nintendo Switch, with 156.59 million units as of June 30, 2026.

How many Switch 2 consoles have been sold? 23.68 million as of June 30, 2026.

How many Wii consoles were sold? 101.63 million.

What is Nintendo's worst-selling home console? The Wii U, at 13.56 million, not counting the Virtual Boy.
